full_judgment: 2. Plaintiff-respondent No. 1 filed the aforesaid suit in the court of the Assistant Judge in the then Upazila Ramu against the appellant and others for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction and alternatively for recovery of possession in respect of 3.32 acres of land appertaining to RS Khatian No. 171, more fully described in the schedule to the plaint. Plaintiff's case, briefly, was that the entire disputed land belonged to two brothers, Jamaluddin and Alimuddin, in equal shares. Although the disputed land was recorded in the CS record pi rights in the name of Jamaluddin alone, Jamaluddin and Alimuddin lived in the same mess and Jamaluddin was the elder of the two brothers. While Jamaluddin and Alimuddin equally possessed the disputed land, Alimuddin died leaving son, Abdul Hamid and daughter, Salema Khatun, as his heirs. Abdul Hamid then kot mortgaged 2 kanis of land to one Badiuddin for a period of 5 years from 1281 to 1285 Mogi Era corresponding to 1919-1924 AD for securing a loan of Taka 38.00 by executing and registering a deed of mortgage on 16-6-1919. Jamaluddin then died leaving son, Abdul Majid and daughter, Saderannessa. Abdul Majid went away to Burma and died there unmarried leaving full sister Sadernncssa and father's brother's son, Abdul Hamid as his heirs. During the RS operation the shares of Saderannessa and Abdul Majid were wrongly recorded in the names of Badiuddin and his brother's son at his instance. In fact, Badiuddin used to possess 2 kanis of land as mortgagee of Abdul Hamid and taking advantage of this fact, Badiuddin got the RS record of rights recorded in his name and in the name of his relations. Abdul Hamid by inheritance as stated above acquired 12 annas share in the disputed land. While Abdul Hamid was in possession of his share he again kot mortgaged the same land to one Kalachand by executing and registering a deed of mortgage on 15-5-1933 and subsequently he redeemed the said mortgage in case No. 606/2 of 1940 before the Special Debt Settlement Board and obtained possession therein. Abdul Hamid then died leaving two sons, namely the plaintiff Haji Golam Bari and Kala Mia and two daughters, Kulsuma Khatun and Omda Khatun and s widow, Sonaban, as his heirs. The plaintiff purchased the shares of his co-sharers including the share of Salema Khatun by different registered kabalas Saderannessa died leaving son, Sahar Mulluk and husband Tamim Golam as her heirs. The defendants, some of whom are the heirs of the first mortgagee, Badiuddin threatened the plaintiff with dispossession. Hence the suit.
